newsitem.title: FRANCE: Norway picks France for patrol boat upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Norway picks France for patrol boat upgrade.

text.p: France's DCN International has won an 850 million crown ($117 million) contract to modernise 14 fast patrol boats for the Norwegian navy, the commercial arm of the state-owned DCN naval shipyard said on Friday.
The Norwegian deal ends two years of competitive tendering from eight leading companies, DCN International said in a statement.

The contract covers the supply of the French SENIT combat management system for Hauk-class patrol vessels, with associated sensors, communications and navigation equipment and an upgrade of the boats.
The first modernised boat will be delivered in the autumn of 2000, with further deliveries falling due every three or four months. DCN International tendered in cooperation with Norway's Kongsberg.

The Norwegian authorities have also taken an option for supply of between six and eight DCN combat systems for a new sea-skimming patrol boat using hydrofoil-type technology. The deal could be worth up to 900 million crowns if parliament votes funds for the Skjold-class vessel, a DCN International spokesman said.
Kvaerner is currently building the Skjold prototype, which will be able to hit speeds of 50 knots with its hull lifting out of the water.
DCN would deliver a system based on SENIT, a highly- automated system which will equip France's Charles de Gaulle nuclear-powered aircraft carrier which enters service in 1999.

The software will link up sensors such as radar, infra-red and optronics, communications and navigation systems, to allow the boats to perform like fighter jets and intercept threats along Norways' fjords, the spokesman said. ($ = 7.254 Norwegian Crowns)
